version.changelog: Audit records the entry point (surface); deny rules written with pre-2.0 tool names keep working

llm.summary: This is a disclosed local audit and policy helper for VMware skills, with sensitive local logs to protect but no artifact evidence of deception or exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: The skill writes local audit, rules, and undo files under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME and detects only the presence of known agent environment variables; this is proportionate to audit infrastructure but creates sensitive local records.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a uv package named vmware-policy and Bash is allowed; the artifact itself is Markdown documentation and does not embed executable payloads, though the runtime package code was not included in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation is somewhat broad because it auto-loads for VMware tool calls and audit/policy questions, but that is consistent with an infrastructure dependency and is disclosed in the skill text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Cross-session local state is explicit and purpose-aligned, including audit.db, rules.yaml, undo.db, rotation, and hot-reload; the documented VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED escape hatch and best-effort audit writes should be controlled by operators.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, audit logging, policy checks, sanitization, and a vmware-audit CLI, matches the documented capabilities; the skill exposes no MCP tools itself and is described as infrastructure for other VMware skills.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you use the VMware skill family and are comfortable with a local audit database that may contain inventory names, configuration details, and redacted operation data. Protect ~/.vmware, review audit exports before sharing them, configure deny rules before relying on policy enforcement, and restrict who can set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED or the MCP host environment.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig, token, and password references are redaction examples for audit rows, not instructions to read credential files.
[PE2] expected: The chmod 700 and chmod 600 commands are local permission-hardening steps for ~/.vmware and audit.db, not sudo or root escalation.
[RA2] expected: Persistent local audit and policy files are disclosed and central to the skill's purpose; no cron job, service, or backdoor-style persistence appears in the artifacts.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited guardrail text discusses how policy rules can require human approval and states no rules ship enabled; it does not instruct autonomous high-impact execution.
[E3] expected: The ls command is a troubleshooting check for a single rules.yaml path, not broad filesystem enumeration.
[SQP-1] expected: The routing condition is broad but expected for a shared VMware audit/policy dependency; users should understand it may load for general audit-log or policy-rule tasks.
